security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, Ssstrict is declared in the ISA string (Parameters.scala:299) but TRAP_ON_UNIMPLEMENTED_INSTRUCTION and TRAP_ON_UNIMPLEMENTED_CSR have no explicit hardware parameter binding. The CSR trap gate relies on LookupTreeDefault in MaskedRegMap.isIllegalAddr (RegMap.scala:60-63) defaulting unmapped CSR addresses to illegal — this is correct but fragile: if a developer adds a reserved CSR address to the mapping with a dummy zero register instead of leaving it unmapped, the access succeeds silently instead of trapping. For instruction decode, illegal-instr trapping depends on the decoder's `ill` output (RvcExpander.scala:36 → ExceptionType.Ill); if the decoder table has gaps in reserved encoding space — i.e., unimplemented standard/reserved opcodes that decode without asserting `ill` — those opcodes will pass through the pipeline without raising an illegal instruction exception, directly violating Ssstrict's requirement that all unimplemented opcodes in standard/reserved space must trap.
security_spec.summary: Ssstrict extension declared in ISA string but no explicit TRAP_ON_UNIMPLEMENTED_* hardware enforcement exists — CSR trapping relies on LookupTreeDefault defaults and instruction trapping relies on decoder ill coverage, both of which are implicit conventions vulnerable to silent regression when reserved encodings are accidentally mapped or decoded as valid.
